dish: Louis Linster's contemporary tasting menu (langoustine; game with exotic spice)
address: 17 Route de Luxembourg, L-5752 Frisange, Luxembourg
w: The former Léa Linster, now run by her son Louis, who took the family table to two MICHELIN stars in 2025 and was Gault&Millau Luxembourg 'Restaurant of the Year 2024'. Classic finesse reworked into minimalist, delicately spiced contemporary plates. One of only two two-star tables in the Grand Duchy.

dish: the plant-forward tasting menu (roots, wild herbs and flowers)
address: AIRFIELD, Findel (near Luxembourg Airport), Findel, Luxembourg
w: René Mathieu's vegetable temple, which earned Luxembourg's first MICHELIN green star for sustainability and has been voted 'best vegetable restaurant in the world' by We're Smart. Roots, flowers and wild herbs foraged from the surrounding nature become edible works of art; relocated from Bourglinster castle to the AIRFIELD near the airport.

dish: polished French gastronomy (Bresse poultry, Dieppe scallops)
address: 9 Place de Clairefontaine, L-1341 Luxembourg (Ville Haute), Luxembourg
w: A MICHELIN-starred institution behind a majestic façade in the heart of the Ville Haute, on the quiet Place de Clairefontaine. Chef Arnaud Magnier is a past-master of polished Gallic fare built on top produce — Bresse poultry, Dieppe scallops.

dish: Cyril Molard's creative French tasting menu
address: 1 Rue de Remich, L-5331 Moutfort, Luxembourg
w: Cyril Molard's snug two-MICHELIN-star table in Moutfort, for years the only two-star in the country. Outstanding produce, subtle tangy acidity and classically leaning sauces that keep the spotlight on the main ingredient.

dish: Fabrice Salvador's seasonal French menu (Bresse poultry, day-boat fish)
address: Hôtel Le Place d'Armes, Place d'Armes, L-1136 Luxembourg (Ville Haute), Luxembourg
w: The MICHELIN-starred dining room of boutique hotel Le Place d'Armes, wrapped in gold leaf and Art Nouveau stained glass. Chef Fabrice Salvador — trained at Troisgros, Guérard and Darroze — cooks seasonal, organic-leaning French cuisine with Bresse poultry and small-boat fish.

dish: Luxembourgish-Asian tasting menu (4/6/8 courses, with a plant-based option)
address: Villa Pétrusse, Luxembourg City (Ville Haute), Luxembourg
w: Inside the restored 1880 Villa Pétrusse, Le Lys won a MICHELIN star less than a year after opening. Luxembourg native Kim De Dood — two stars at Saint-Pierre in Singapore — blends traditional Luxembourgish cuisine with big-boned Asian intensity.

dish: izakaya-style sharing plates and kaiseki (premium sashimi)
address: Rue Münster, L-2160 Luxembourg (Grund), Luxembourg
w: Luxembourg's first Japanese restaurant, founded 1988 in the Grund and long in the MICHELIN Guide. Reinvented as 'Aké by Kamakura' with izakaya-style sharing menus, chef Akira Yasuoka works premium product into timeless recipes with no concession to Western tastes.

dish: the epic mezze platter (15 mezze, dips and pâtés)
address: 46 Place Guillaume II, L-1648 Luxembourg (Ville Haute), Luxembourg
w: A MICHELIN Bib Gourmand on central Place Guillaume II, cool and chic, built around Mediterranean and Middle-Eastern mezze — an array of up to 15 appetisers, dips and pâtés for sharing. The most accessible credentialled table in the city.

dish: François Jagut's inventive French cuisine
address: Rue Théodore Flammang, L-5618 Mondorf-les-Bains, Luxembourg
w: The gastronomic table of Casino 2000 in the spa town of Mondorf-les-Bains, where Breton chef François Jagut — Gault&Millau Luxembourg 'Chef of the Year 2025' — serves inventive, fresh French cuisine with award-winning sommelier Thierry Corona on wine.

dish: refined French garden-veranda tasting menu
address: Place Sainte-Cunégonde, Luxembourg City (Clausen), Luxembourg
w: A MICHELIN-starred restaurant with rooms in historic Clausen, five minutes from the centre. Gourmet dining under a veranda or on a terrace overlooking the garden's vines and a water feature, run by Annabelle Hazard and Pascal Soutiran.

dish: Julien Lucas's Gallic menu (Brittany lobster, Provence asparagus)
n: La Villa de Camille et Julien
address: Belair, Luxembourg City, Luxembourg
w: A one-MICHELIN-star table in leafy Belair. Chef Julien Lucas — trained alongside Robuchon, Loiseau and Ducasse — builds precise plates on high-quality Gallic ingredients like Brittany lobster and Provence asparagus.

dish: hearty classic French (foie gras, scallops, cream and butter)
address: 17 Rue de la Résistance, L-4996 Schouweiler, Luxembourg
w: A family-run one-MICHELIN-star restaurant in an old stone house in Schouweiler with an exquisite garden terrace. Founded by Pierrick Guillou and continued by the chefs he trained; authenticity and intensity — lashings of cream and butter, foie gras and scallops.

dish: steak tartare with Thai notes; risotto with truffle and skate-wing fritter
address: Parc Le'h, Dudelange, Luxembourg
w: A MICHELIN Bib Gourmand brasserie in wood and natural materials, in osmosis with the Dudelange forest. Chef Jean-Charles Albert's pared-back cooking is subtle and often surprising — steak tartare with oriental notes, creamy risotto with truffle and skate.

dish: Baptiste Heugens's contemporary tasting menu
address: Route d'Arlon, L-8010 Strassen, Luxembourg
w: A contemporary gastronomic table in Strassen rated three toques by Gault&Millau, with chef Baptiste Heugens turning out refined, modern cooking. Among the higher-scoring kitchens in the Grand Duchy.

dish: classic, generous French gastronomy
address: 10 Rue de la Gare, L-5690 Ellange, Luxembourg
w: A prettily renovated old railway station in Ellange-Gare, run for more than 40 years by Daniel Rameau, president of Euro-Toques Luxembourg. Classic, generous, indulgent gastronomy by an open fire.

dish: convivial sharing bistro plates; 50+ gins
address: 6 Plateau Altmünster, L-1123 Luxembourg (Clausen), Luxembourg
w: An unpretentious yet trendy French bistro in Clausen (14/20 Gault&Millau), with a menu built for sharing, a bar of more than 50 gins and a lovely back terrace in fine weather.

dish: Judd mat Gaardebounen and other Luxembourgish classics
address: Place d'Armes, L-1136 Luxembourg (Ville Haute), Luxembourg
w: A brasserie on the Place d'Armes serving typical Luxembourgish dishes — Judd mat Gaardebounen among them — alongside wood-fired pizza and coffee specialities, at fair prices in the heart of the old town.

dish: regional Luxembourgish specialities with Moselle wines
address: 9 Berreggaass, L-5485 Wormeldange-Haut, Luxembourg
w: A historic inn (est. 1907) atop the Wormerberg in the Moselle wine village of Wormeldange, with panoramic terrace views over the vineyards and river. Traditional Luxembourgish and regional specialities and, as an 'Ambassadeur des Vins et Crémants de la Moselle', a deep list of Luxembourg Moselle wines.

dish: tagliatelle alla grana finished tableside in a Parmesan wheel
address: 6 Rue du Fort Niedergrünewald, L-2226 Luxembourg (Kirchberg), Luxembourg
w: An authentic trattoria in the Kirchberg business district (at the Sofitel Europe), where chef Rodolfo Serritelli's signature tagliatelle alla grana is finished tableside in a wheel of Parmesan.

dish: flat white / cappuccino (The Barn beans) with kanelbullar
address: 101 Rue Adolphe Fischer, L-1521 Luxembourg (Gare), Luxembourg
w: A cosy specialty coffee shop in the Gare quarter pulling shots from Berlin master-roaster The Barn, with a case of kanelbullar, pistachio buns and vegan cakes. A fixture of Luxembourg's third-wave scene.

dish: single-origin filter and espresso from the in-house roastery
address: Hollerich, Luxembourg City, Luxembourg
w: A pioneering Luxembourg roaster (since 2002), its main Hollerich site a former mechanic's garage filled with plants, plus cafés in Gare and the Ville Haute. Serious single-origin filter and espresso from beans roasted in-house.

dish: biodynamic/natural wines by the glass with cheese and charcuterie
address: Grund, Luxembourg City, Luxembourg
w: A charming natural-wine bar in the Grund run by Rossi Petkova and Franz Dickes, pouring from some 730 organic and biodynamic wines across 18 countries — including the Luxembourg Moselle — with seasonal French plates, cheese and charcuterie.

dish: trio de bacalhau (à Brás, à Braga and à Lagareiro)
address: 90 Dernier Sol, L-2543 Luxembourg (Bonnevoie), Luxembourg
w: Long held up as the best of Luxembourg's many Portuguese restaurants, a five-minute walk from the station in Bonnevoie. Extensive fish and seafood, with an outstanding trio de bacalhau. Luxembourg's large Portuguese community shows on the plate.

dish: espada (black scabbard fish) with banana; espetada Madeirense
address: Ville Haute, Luxembourg City, Luxembourg
w: A specialist in the cooking of Madeira — deep-fried black scabbard fish with banana and passion-fruit sauce, espetada on a bay-leaf skewer, bolo do caco — beautifully presented, a favourite of the city's Portuguese and Madeiran diaspora.

dish: handcrafted pralines and bean-to-bar chocolate
address: Luxembourg City, Luxembourg
w: A family-run artisan chocolate maker turning out very high-quality handcrafted pralines and bars — a stop on Luxembourg's small but serious chocolate map.

dish: hot-chocolate spoon dipped in warm milk
address: Rue du Marché-aux-Herbes, L-1728 Luxembourg (Ville Haute), Luxembourg
w: A much-loved café in a 15th-century building directly opposite the Grand Ducal Palace. The signature is the chocolate spoon — pick a flavour from the display, dip it in a jug of hot milk — plus generous brunches. A homegrown Luxembourg brand that has since expanded.

dish: tonkotsu / shoyu ramen
address: Rue Sainte-Zithe, L-2763 Luxembourg (Gare), Luxembourg
w: A tiny, wildly popular ramen bar near the station — reservations advised, especially at lunch — turning out proper tonkotsu and shoyu bowls. A high point of Luxembourg's growing Japanese-street-food scene.

dish: miso / tonkotsu / shoyu ramen with fresh noodles
address: Place de Paris, L-2314 Luxembourg (Gare), Luxembourg
w: A ramen specialist on Place de Paris where you build a bowl from miso, tonkotsu or shoyu broths with fresh noodles and toppings — part of the Gare quarter's cluster of good Japanese kitchens.

dish: free-range beef burger with homemade bun
address: Luxembourg City, Luxembourg
w: From the Black Sheep group, a short, well-balanced burger menu built on free-range beef and homemade bread, with everything from classic fries to sweet-potato fries — a repeat pick in the city's burger round-ups.

dish: mezze — hummus, falafel, halloumi (BYOB)
address: Limpertsberg, Luxembourg City, Luxembourg
w: A warm, family Lebanese kitchen in Limpertsberg — 'Good & Honest Food' — built for sharing plenty of small mezze plates: perfect falafel, hummus, halloumi, couscous. No alcohol served but BYOB with no corkage, at very fair prices.

dish: bò bún and traditional pho
address: 2 Place Léon XIII, L-1929 Luxembourg (Bonnevoie), Luxembourg
w: A hidden treasure in Bonnevoie a stone's throw from the central station, widely credited with the best bò bún in Luxembourg — plus scented pho and crispy egg rolls.
